rounds.proof_sketch: With K=2949: TILE_K=8 iterates 369 times covering indices 0-2951 (2949-2951 zero-padded); TILE_K=7 iterates 422 times covering indices 0-2953 (2949-2953 zero-padded). Both sum exactly the same K=2949 valid elements. Additionally, forward() has a safety fallback that returns torch.matmul if custom kernel differs by >1e-4, masking any potential difference.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes TILE_K from 8 to 7, affecting the internal tiling stride over the K dimension. However, both versions correctly process all K=2949 elements through their respective loop iterations, with boundary handling zero-padding invalid indices. The mathematical sum Σ A[i,k]*B[k,j] for k=0 to K-1 remains identical. Furthermore, the forward() function contains an explicit correctness check that falls back to torch.matmul if the custom kernel differs significantly, creating a safety net that masks any kernel-level difference. The 112 rounds of bitwise-identical testing confirms semantic equivalence.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation affects tiling stride but not the mathematical result. The K-loop correctly covers all elements with both tile sizes, and the fallback mechanism ensures correctness regardless.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing kernels with host-level safety fallbacks, explicitly test the raw kernel output without the fallback mechanism to detect semantic differences in the kernel itself. Also consider adding assertions that verify the kernel is actually being used (no fallback triggered) to catch efficiency-correctness tradeoffs.
